archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm-dependent)
archetype.definition: A pure pocket thrower who has not scrambled once this year. He wins on timing throws short and over the middle, and his output rises and falls with how cleanly the offense stays on schedule around him.

report.headline: Accuracy has slipped back below even his pre-2025 self; Week 4 hints at recovery
report.take:
Jordan Love arrived in 2026 off the best year of his career. In 2025 he was fifth in EPA per play (0.287) and eighth in CPOE (+5.5), with a bad-throw rate of 12.5% that finally matched his arm talent. He has never been a runner in any real volume, and this year he is purely a pocket passer: zero scrambles, six carries for -8 yards. That means everything rides on the arm, and through four games the arm has been the problem.

The core issue is accuracy, and it is not only protection. His CPOE of -6.6 ranks 36th of 42. His bad-throw rate of 18.8% is 30th of 32 and worse than his 2023 and 2024 levels (16.9% and 17.2%), never mind 2025. Week 1 at Minnesota, the league's top defense, is easy to excuse: he was pressured on 47.8% of dropbacks and 37.5% of his throws were off-target. Week 2 is not: the Jets pressured him only 15.6% of the time, and he still finished at -13.6 CPOE. The environment makes it harder. Green Bay's run game is dead last in EPA (-0.406), so Love lives on long third downs: 7.8 yards to go on average, a 26.2% conversion rate and -0.342 EPA per play. He is also releasing the ball faster than ever (2.48 seconds, against 2.77-2.89 the last three years) and taking fewer tight-window throws. That reads like a passer hurrying through a pocket he doesn't trust.

The raw totals flatter him in places and undersell him in others. The 387 yards in Week 1 came with -2.7 EPA, and 312 yards in Week 3 took 53 attempts in a 21-point loss. Altogether, 57 of his 162 dropbacks came while trailing by nine or more. The eight touchdowns, two in every game, rest on seven red-zone scores even though his red-zone EPA is negative. Underneath that, his best football is real. Throws of 10-19 air yards produce 0.257 EPA with a 52.9% success rate. Under center, play-action territory for this offense, he is at 0.193 EPA and +5.3 CPOE, against roughly break-even from shotgun.

Week 4 at Tampa, a top-five defense, was the template: 22 of 30, +5.3 CPOE, 6.9 EPA, no sacks. That looked like the 2025 version. The supporting cast is getting thinner, though. Starting center Jacob Monk and guard Aaron Banks are out, tackle Zach Bako-Bewele and receiver Jayden Reed are on IR, and the offense already allows hits at the second-worst rate in the league. Expect the accuracy to drift back toward neutral, because a four-game crater against a strong career record usually does. A full return to last year's level is unlikely without a run game to keep him ahead of the sticks.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws are his money zone
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards are his most productive area by a wide margin, with the best EPA and success rate of any depth. Throws over the middle carry the highest success rate of any direction. This is timing and anticipation into windows, the part of his game that made 2025 work, and it should hold. The two interceptions at this depth are the cost of throwing there.

strengths.title: Sharp under center
strengths.body: From under center he completes 66.7% of his throws, above expectation, and produces 0.193 EPA per play, against slightly negative EPA from shotgun. That points to play-action and run-game marriage as the way to keep him comfortable. It is only 31 plays, so it is a hint rather than a fact. It is also the clearest lever the coaches have.

strengths.title: Career record says accuracy rebounds
strengths.body: Love has posted a positive CPOE in each of his last three full seasons, peaking at +5.5 with a top-five EPA in 2025. A four-game -6.6 against that history is more likely a slump than a new baseline. Week 4's +5.3 CPOE and 6.9 EPA against a top-five defense is the first sign of the snap-back.

concerns.title: Inaccuracy that isn't just pressure
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate ranks near the bottom of the league and is worse than any full season he has played as a starter. It showed up even in Week 2, when the Jets barely pressured him and he still finished at -13.6 CPOE. Some of this is quicker, rushed releases behind a shaky line, but part of it is his own mechanics. It is the main reason his EPA sits 25th despite good volume.

concerns.title: Living behind the sticks
concerns.body: The league's worst rushing offense by EPA leaves Love facing third downs at 7.8 yards to go on average. He converts barely a quarter of them, with deeply negative EPA. This is mostly the offense's doing, not his. Until the run game finds anything, his down-and-distance will keep dragging on his efficiency.

concerns.title: Patchwork protection getting thinner
concerns.body: Green Bay already ranks 31st in hits allowed. Now center Jacob Monk (96% of snaps) and guard Aaron Banks are out, and tackle Zach Bako-Bewele is on IR. Love turns 21.6% of pressures into sacks and has four turnover-worthy fumbles. A reshuffled interior is exactly what speeds up a passer who is already releasing early.

trend.note: His pass EPA has climbed every week from Week 2 on: -2.7, -3.2, +3.6, +6.9. Week 4's 22 of 30 with zero sacks was his cleanest game, though it came on only 197 yards in a low-total game.

nextGame.headline: Bears smother the short game but leak deep shots
nextGame.body:
Chicago's defense is built to take away what Love does most. It ranks second against the pass by EPA and second on short throws (-0.253), and 100 of his 154 attempts have gone behind the line or under 10 air yards. The Bears also sack quarterbacks at the fourth-highest rate. They have held quarterbacks to 210.3 yards a game, third-fewest, while still allowing 1.5 touchdowns. The crack is downfield: Chicago is 28th in deep EPA and 22nd in explosive pass rate allowed. That is the one area where Love has been poor, completing 5 of 20 at 20+ air yards. Their run defense is also 27th by EPA, a rare chance for Green Bay's ground game to keep him on schedule.

Availability cuts both ways. Green Bay goes in without center Jacob Monk and guard Aaron Banks, with Bako-Bewele and Jayden Reed on IR. That narrows Love to Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft, with Skyy Moore's -0.272 EPA per target the fallback. Chicago is without quarterback Caleb Williams (week-to-week) and left tackle Braxton Jones (IR), which should help the game script. Its secondary is also thinned: corner Cam Lewis (84% of snaps) and safety Anthony Johnson Jr. are out. Kyler Gordon is listed out despite an Oct. 1 note calling him a full participant, so check his final status.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into Chicago's strength
keyMatchups.body: Love's volume lives underneath, and Chicago allows almost nothing there. If Green Bay stays in a quick-game shell, expect another inefficient day of check-downs and long third downs. The under-center, play-action looks are the way around it.

keyMatchups.title: Watson vs. a depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: Chicago is 28th in deep EPA and missing Cam Lewis and Anthony Johnson Jr. Christian Watson's 0.312 EPA per target leads Love's receivers. The question is whether Love can hit throws he has completed only 25% of the time, or 5 of 20.

keyMatchups.title: Patched interior vs. Bears rush
keyMatchups.body: A fourth-ranked sack rate meets a line missing its starting center and a guard, already 31st in hits allowed. Interior pressure is what pushes Love's release earlier and his accuracy lower.

nextGame.watch: Whether Green Bay can run against Chicago's 27th-ranked run defense and get Love under center on manageable downs. If it can't, his third-down numbers will drag the day down again.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the accuracy to recover partway. A CPOE near zero, rather than -6.6 or last year's +5.5, fits his three-year record and his improving weekly trend. The yardage pace of about 260 a game was padded by two trailing scripts and should cool. So should the two-touchdown-every-week streak, because his red-zone efficiency is negative and seven scores on 25 red-zone attempts leans on frequent trips more than sharp play. What is sustainable is the intermediate game and the under-center efficiency.

The ceiling depends on the supporting cast. A last-ranked run game and an injury-thinned line keep him behind schedule, and Reed's absence narrows the receiver group. If Monk returns and the ground game climbs out of the cellar, a 2025-style stretch is possible. If not, he is a mid-pack efficiency passer whose volume depends on game script.
swingFactors: Monk's return and interior line health
Any life in a last-ranked run game

bets.reason: Chicago allows the third-fewest quarterback yards (210.3) and ranks second against the pass. Love's average is inflated by 387- and 312-yard games built in losing scripts. With Chicago's quarterback out, a trailing script is less likely.
Green Bay is averaging 18.25 points with the 26th-ranked offense, against a top-five defense, while Chicago is without Caleb Williams. Green Bay's defense allows the fourth-fewest explosive passes.

Green Bay is at home in a division game catching a field goal against a team without its starting quarterback and left tackle. The Packers are 0-3-1 against the spread and their offense has struggled with good defenses, so this is only a slight edge.
He has thrown exactly two in every game, but his red-zone EPA is negative. Chicago allows 1.5 quarterback touchdowns a game behind the league's second-best pass defense.

confidence.note: Four-game sample against a strong career record, with offensive line injuries clouding the read.
